editing_process: Highly collaborative, focus on voice-driven intimacy. Deep dives into character motivation; she pushes authors to make their interior monologues more rigorous and authentic.
likes: Unforced prose, psychological interiority, emotional honesty, narratives that feel inevitable rather than constructed.
dislikes: Self-conscious stylistic flourishes, sentimentality, characters that lack clear agency, 'plotty' prose that lacks soul.
editorial_sensibility: The 'advocate'—she looks for books that she can champion as essential; values long-term career building over the 'hot' book of the moment.
public_record_insights: Known for her work with authors like Karen Russell and Louise Erdrich; focuses on the rhythm of the sentence as an extension of the character’s thought process.
notable_books: The Goldfinch by Donna Tartt
Homegoing by Yaa Gyasi
The Sellout by Paul Beatty
Swamplandia! by Karen Russell

editing_process: Structural architect. Spends significant time on the 'macro'—pacing, character arcs, and the structural integrity of the narrative frame before addressing line edits.
likes: Narrative urgency, clarity of vision, stories that hook the reader immediately, structural innovation that serves the plot.
dislikes: Flabby midsections, lack of stakes, protagonists who remain static, overly dense or opaque prose that obscures the emotional center.
editorial_sensibility: The 'architect'—believes that if the structure is solid, the prose will have the space to shine. Values a propulsive, undeniable reading experience.
public_record_insights: Often praised for her ability to untangle complex manuscript webs; focuses heavily on how a book moves through time.
notable_books: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao by Junot Díaz
A Visit from the Goon Squad by Jennifer Egan
Wild by Cheryl Strayed

editing_process: Legendarily meticulous. Known for his 'green pen' method; line-by-line, word-by-word surgical precision. He focuses on tightening the prose until only the essential remains.
likes: Economy, minimalism, precision, muscular prose, authentic dialogue that sounds like real speech.
dislikes: Adverb-heavy writing, lack of restraint, melodrama, decorative prose that doesn't advance the narrative.
editorial_sensibility: The 'purist'—believes in the erasure of the author's ego; the goal is for the prose to feel as if it simply exists, without visible effort.
public_record_insights: Famous for long-standing collaborations (e.g., Haruki Murakami, Cormac McCarthy); viewed as the gold standard for high-literary discipline.
notable_books: The Secret History by Donna Tartt
Blood Meridian by Cormac McCarthy
Norwegian Wood by Haruki Murakami
Less Than Zero by Bret Easton Ellis

editing_process: Strategic and editorially involved. Focuses on the intersection of cultural relevance and narrative craft; works closely on positioning and voice.
likes: Literary-commercial hybrids, books with 'voice' that feel urgent, narratives that engage with contemporary social dynamics.
dislikes: Isolationist fiction that feels detached from the real world, clunky exposition, characters that function as stand-ins for ideology.
editorial_sensibility: The 'cultural curator'—seeks books that will start conversations. Values books that demand to be read now.
public_record_insights: Known for bridging the gap between high-art and the marketplace; excels at making challenging literary concepts accessible.
notable_books: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao by Junot Díaz
The Reluctant Fundamentalist by Mohsin Hamid
The Sympathizer by Viet Thanh Nguyen

editing_process: Deep emotional engagement. She acts as the ultimate 'first reader,' focusing on the moral and emotional stakes of the book.
likes: The 'cultural artifact'—books that feel like they will endure, complex human relationships, intellectual depth.
dislikes: Superficiality, books that rely on shock value, lack of thematic resonance.
editorial_sensibility: The 'guardian'—views publishing as a stewardship of literature. Looks for the rare book that has both immediate impact and longevity.
public_record_insights: Long-time editor of Don DeLillo and Stephen King; balances the profound with the popular with unparalleled skill.
notable_books: Underworld by Don DeLillo
All the Light We Cannot See by Anthony Doerr
The Shining by Stephen King

editing_process: Aesthetic-focused. Operates at a high-literary level where the quality of the sentence is the primary metric of success.
likes: Strange/idiosyncratic voices, linguistic innovation, experimental structures, prose that defies categorization.
dislikes: Convention for the sake of convention, 'market-tested' formulas, sloppy or un-curated prose.
editorial_sensibility: The 'aesthete'—prioritizes the singular vision of the author above all else. If it's weird and brilliant, she wants it.
public_record_insights: Renowned for her uncompromising taste; she champions work that pushes the boundaries of what a novel can be.
notable_books: Normal People by Sally Rooney
Dept. of Speculation by Jenny Offill
Bluets by Maggie Nelson

editing_process: Intellectually intensive. Engages with the 'big ideas' of the manuscript; pushes the author to sharpen their arguments and world-building.
likes: High-concept literary fiction, books that demand intellectual rigor, unique world-views, challenging narrative structures.
dislikes: Lazy world-building, lack of ambition, prose that takes the 'easy road'.
editorial_sensibility: The 'provocateur'—seeks out books that challenge the reader and change the way they look at the world.
public_record_insights: Known for his work with complex literary voices; enjoys the intersection of philosophy and fiction.
notable_books: Submission by Michel Houellebecq
The Sellout by Paul Beatty
10:04 by Ben Lerner

editing_process: Thematic deep-dives. Focuses on the 'why' of the book; ensures the moral and social framework of the story holds up under scrutiny.
likes: Socially engaged fiction, intellectual complexity, historical depth, nuanced character studies.
dislikes: Simplistic black-and-white moralizing, lack of intellectual rigor, characters that lack agency.
editorial_sensibility: The 'intellectual'—values the book as a way of exploring the human condition. Always looks for the 'why' beneath the 'what.'
public_record_insights: Widely respected for his work on books that tackle heavy, serious subjects with grace and precision.
notable_books: The Corrections by Jonathan Franzen
The Known World by Edward P. Jones
Gilead by Marilynne Robinson

editing_process: Urgency-driven. Asks 'why does this book need to exist right now?' Edits with a focus on the moral weight and social relevance of the work.
likes: Narratives with 'teeth,' social commentary, urgent/necessary stories, clear-eyed prose.
dislikes: Apathy, lack of consequence, stories that don't have something to say.
editorial_sensibility: The 'witness'—looks for books that bear witness to the world we live in. Values courage in writing.
public_record_insights: Often seeks out voices that have been marginalized or have something challenging to say about the state of the world.
notable_books: The Glass Castle by Jeannette Walls
Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil by John Berendt
The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks by Rebecca Skloot

editing_process: Voice-centric. Identifies the 'strange' and pulls it to the surface; helps the author amplify their unique creative DNA.
likes: Distinctive, inimitable voices, the 'beautifully strange,' emotional anchors in speculative worlds.
dislikes: Derivativeness, safe choices, prose that feels like it was written to please everyone.
editorial_sensibility: The 'discoverer'—looks for the spark of originality that makes an author stand out in a crowded market.
public_record_insights: Known for her championing of unique literary stylists; she is not afraid of the 'weird'.
notable_books: The Goldfinch by Donna Tartt
The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo by Stieg Larsson
The Interestings by Meg Wolitzer

editing_process: Market-aware but literary-driven. Focuses on the balance between a compelling 'hook' and authentic character development.
likes: Compulsive readability, complex character work, 'book club' fiction with literary ambition.
dislikes: Boredom, lack of plot movement, 'empty' prose that lacks character depth.
editorial_sensibility: The 'balancer'—knows how to keep a book accessible to a broad audience while maintaining high literary standards.
public_record_insights: Highly sought after for her ability to turn literary books into broad successes; emphasizes the reader’s experience.
notable_books: Room by Emma Donoghue
I Am Malala by Malala Yousafzai
Homeland Elegies by Ayad Akhtar

editing_process: Big-picture focused. Encourages authors to expand their scope; looks at the cultural and social implications of the narrative.
likes: Ambitious scopes, cultural criticism, big-idea fiction, historical resonance.
dislikes: Small/petty concerns, lack of ambition, prose that feels closed-off or claustrophobic.
editorial_sensibility: The 'visionary'—looks for the books that will define the cultural moment. Values scale and depth.
public_record_insights: Works frequently with writers who are also thinkers or critics; values the intersection of intellect and art.
notable_books: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao by Junot Díaz
The Sense of an Ending by Julian Barnes
The Year of Magical Thinking by Joan Didion

editing_process: Direct and frank. Believes in a strong, long-term editorial relationship; cuts through the noise to get to the heart of the author's intent.
likes: Historical realism, emotional authenticity, character-driven narrative arcs, clean prose.
dislikes: Artifice, melodrama, sentimentality, characters that aren't 'real'.
editorial_sensibility: The 'straight-shooter'—known for her candid, high-commitment editing style. She is in the trenches with her authors.
public_record_insights: Known for her success with high-profile biographical and historical fiction; values truth above comfort.
notable_books: The Emperor of All Maladies by Siddhartha Mukherjee
The Known World by Edward P. Jones
The Corrections by Jonathan Franzen

editing_process: Meticulous and broad-reaching. Works with large, sprawling manuscripts; focuses on structure, pacing, and historical/cultural grounding.
likes: Ambitious scope, masterful prose, research-heavy narratives, complex sprawling worlds.
dislikes: Inaccuracy, lack of research, thin characters, plot holes.
editorial_sensibility: The 'classical heavyweight'—prized for her ability to wrangle massive, complex books into coherent, brilliant novels.
public_record_insights: A legendary editor who excels at the 'big book'—the kind that defines a career.
notable_books: The Poisonwood Bible by Barbara Kingsolver
The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay by Michael Chabon
A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles

editing_process: Pacing-focused. Works to ensure the momentum of the book is unrelenting while keeping the prose high-quality.
likes: Propulsive storytelling, high-stakes narratives, sharp dialogue, 'unputdownable' quality.
dislikes: Slow beginnings, meandering plots, lack of tension, repetitive prose.
editorial_sensibility: The 'powerhouse'—focuses on the reader’s engagement. She knows how to build a book that keeps people reading until 3 AM.
public_record_insights: Known for identifying commercial potential in literary fiction; she understands the 'pulse' of a story.
notable_books: The Help by Kathryn Stockett
The Devil Wears Prada by Lauren Weisberger
Where the Crawdads Sing by Delia Owens
